title: Lamphun With Kids: 2-Day Family Itinerary, Thailand | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 2-day, 1-night Lamphun family itinerary for kids in northern Thailand: pay respects at Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, ride the old-town tram, try weaving at Ban Nong Ngueak, and unwind at a rice-field cafe.
keywords: Lamphun with kids, Lamphun family trip, Lamphun 2-day itinerary, Ban Nong Ngueak weaving, Lamphun tram
h1:
Lamphun With the Family
Temples, Rice Fields, Hand-Woven Cloth
intro: Lamphun is a small town you can drive around in under ten minutes, with all the sights packed close together, so it's an easy place to bring kids without anyone getting cranky from long car rides. We've laid this out as 2 days and 1 night, mixing old Lanna temples, a tram tour of the town, a hands-on weaving session with the Yong community at Ban Nong Ngueak, and a rice-field cafe at the end where the kids can run around.

blocks.html: What makes Lamphun work for families is that everything is close together. You can walk a loop of the old town in a few minutes, and the main temples, the museum, and the monument all sit within a few hundred meters of each other, so kids don't have to sit in the car for long. The weaving village and the rice-field cafes are only a 20–30 minute drive out of town. This plan builds in an afternoon break to head back to the hotel for a nap, then heads out to a cafe once the sun has eased off.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Old town, temples, tram ride

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Lamphun old town · temples · tram tour

items.activity: Arrive in Lamphun, check in at a hotel in town or drop your bags
items.note: Coming from Chiang Mai it's only about a 40-minute drive, so an early start is easy.

items.activity: Wat Phra That Hariphunchai to pay respects at the golden chedi, the heart of the town
items.note: The temple grounds are wide and easy for kids to wander; there's an old bell they can try ringing. Dress modestly with knees and shoulders covered.

items.activity: Ride the old-town tram, with the morning run leaving from in front of Wat Phra That
items.note: The tram passes around 11 key spots, and kids love the open sides. The morning run is around 09:30, so double-check the time on the day.

items.activity: Lunch of khao soi or khanom jeen nam ngiao in town
items.note: There's a good choice of northern Thai spots around the old town, and you can order a non-spicy dish on the side for the kids.

items.activity: Hariphunchai National Museum, across from Wat Phra That
items.note: This was the first national museum in the North. It's air-conditioned and cool, and you can walk through the Buddha images and antiquities without it dragging on, so kids stay interested.

items.activity: Head back to the hotel for the kids to nap during the hottest part of the day
items.note: Lamphun afternoons get hot. An hour and a half of rest, then heading out in the evening, works better.

items.activity: Queen Chamadevi Monument + a stroll and photos around the old town
items.note: Queen Chamadevi was the first ruler of Hariphunchai, which makes a nice spot to tell the kids a short version of the town's story.

items.activity: Dinner at the evening market / food spots around town
items.note: Pick a place with seating and kid-friendly food, like noodles or rice soup.

blocks.title: A tip about the tram
blocks.html: The old-town tram runs a limited number of times a day, and departure times can shift with the season. Call ahead or ask at the square in front of Wat Phra That first. If you miss a run, the town is small enough that you can easily drive or rent bikes and do the loop yourself.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Ban Nong Ngueak weaving + rice-field cafe

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Pa Sang · try weaving · rice-field cafe

items.activity: Check out, have breakfast, then drive to Ban Nong Ngueak in Pa Sang district
items.note: It's about 20–30 minutes from Lamphun town, a Yong community that weaves cotton dyed with natural colors.

items.activity: Walk through Ban Nong Ngueak and watch the grandmothers weaving on real looms
items.note: The village is quiet and calm, with old wooden houses. Kids get to see real daily life, not a staged show.

items.activity: Try a weaving activity / making patterns with the women's group
items.note: Some groups let you try weaving or making patterns; it's best to contact the community in advance (there's a number for the village head). Older kids find it fun.

items.activity: Stop by the Thai Yong Museum, across from Wat Nong Ngueak
items.note: It keeps old Yong tools and belongings and tells the story of the Yong people who migrated and settled here. A short walk-through.

items.activity: Buy hand-woven cotton as a souvenir straight from the community
items.note: Buying from the villagers gets you a better price and puts the money in the weavers' hands. A small scarf starts in the low hundreds of THB.

items.activity: Lunch, then drive back toward town
Rice-field cafe / garden for the kids to run around
items.note: Lamphun has several cafes out in the fields, and some have a small play area for kids, like Safari Garden Playground & Cafe, a good spot to let the kids burn off energy before heading home.

items.activity: Stop for dried or fresh longan as a souvenir, then head home
items.note: Lamphun is longan country, and in July–August fresh longan fills the whole town.

blocks.title: Contact the community before you go
blocks.html: For the weaving activity at Ban Nong Ngueak, it's best to call ahead, since the women's group doesn't run demonstrations every day. Calling the community or checking with the Lamphun municipality / TAT before you set off will save you a wasted trip.

items: Sights close together — you can walk or drive a loop of the old town in a few minutes, so kids aren't stuck in the car long enough to get cranky.
Fewer crowds — the temples and museum aren't as packed as Chiang Mai, making it easy to walk around with kids.
Hands-on activities — ringing the bell at the temple, trying weaving at the village; kids get to do things, not just look.
Rice-field cafes to run around — many have a lawn or a kids' corner where children can burn off energy after a walk.
Close to Chiang Mai — only about a 40-minute drive, so you can tack it onto a Chiang Mai trip, and if the kids tire out it's easy to head back.

blocks.text: Getting ready to travel with kids

blocks.html: Lamphun is hot and sunny during the day, especially in the hot season, so pack hats, sunscreen, and drinking water for the kids. Schedule outdoor activities for the morning and evening, and leave the afternoon for a break. Temples require modest dress with knees and shoulders covered, for adults and older kids alike. Having your own car is by far the easiest option, since the weaving village and the cafes are outside town, and public transport in the province is limited.

items.name: Pack the essentials for kids
items.blurb: Hats, drinking water, snacks, and comfortable walking shoes, since you'll be on your feet in the temple grounds and the village.

items.name: Pick a hotel in town
items.blurb: Staying in the old-town area keeps you close to temples and restaurants, and makes it easy to head back for the kids' midday rest.

faq.q: Can you visit Lamphun with young children?
faq.a: Easily. Lamphun is a small town where the sights sit close together, so kids don't have to ride in the car for long. The temples have wide grounds to wander, and some rice-field cafes are set up as play gardens for kids, like Safari Garden, where they can burn off energy.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Lamphun?
faq.a: Two days and one night is just right for a family. The first day covers the old town, temples, and the tram, and the second day heads out to the weaving village and a rice-field cafe. If you only have one day, you can stick to the old town.

faq.q: Can you actually try weaving at Ban Nong Ngueak, and do you need to book?
faq.a: Yes. Ban Nong Ngueak is a Yong community that weaves cotton dyed with natural colors, and some groups let you try weaving or making patterns. But they don't demonstrate every day, so it's best to call the community to arrange it before you go.

faq.q: How long does it take to get to Lamphun from Chiang Mai?
faq.a: It's about a 40-minute drive from Chiang Mai into Lamphun town, which makes it an easy add-on to a Chiang Mai trip, or a day trip out and back. But if you want to try weaving and sit at a cafe too, it's worth staying overnight.

faq.q: What time of year is best to bring kids to Lamphun?
faq.a: Late rainy season into early cool season (October–February) has the nicest weather, with green rice fields. July–August is longan season, with fresh longan all over town, but the days are hot, so avoid outdoor activities in the afternoon.
